memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Six days do your work, but on the seventh day do not work, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and so that the slave born in your household and the foreigner living among you may be refreshed." - Exodus 23:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God commands a weekly rhythm of rest, and look at how far His care reaches. The Sabbath was not only for the landowner but for the servant, the foreigner, and even the working animals. Everyone and everything under one's care was to be refreshed. God's rest is a gift that spreads to the whole household, especially to those who would otherwise be worked without mercy. Rest, in God's design, is an act of compassion.

In a world that measured people by their usefulness, this was radical. A servant was not a machine to be run without pause; God insisted they be refreshed too. The Sabbath declared that every person has dignity and needs rest, regardless of their status. God cares that the lowest in the household gets to breathe, to recover, to be human again.

We live in a culture that struggles to rest and often resents it as wasted time. But God, who Himself rested after creation, built rest into the very fabric of life as a good and holy thing. It is a weekly declaration that we are not our own gods and that the world does not depend on our endless effort. Jesus said the Sabbath was made for people, not people for the Sabbath (Mark 2:27). Rest is not laziness; it is trust and worship. And it reminds us to extend that same gift of rest to those who serve under us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I honour rhythms of rest, or resent rest as wasted time?
Am I ensuring that those who work under me also get to rest?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the gift of rest. Help me embrace it as trust and worship, and to extend that same refreshment to everyone under my care. Amen.
